goal: Add independent language-aware component and assembled-project quality validation to the reviewed Provider generation route, revalidate cached modules, and reject the known broken CS Demo frontend before downstream integration or delivery.
acceptance_criteria: A separate component quality-validation receipt is produced after module assembly and before the component can feed downstream generation.
JavaScript and TypeScript local imports and re-exports record exact symbols and reject missing exports, missing local re-export bindings, missing modules, and unimported sibling helpers.
Previously passing component checkpoints are revalidated against the current quality contract before reuse.
Python syntax and implemented import interfaces plus JSON syntax are rechecked at component scope without relying on provider self-claims.
The fully merged project receives an assembly quality validation and generation cannot report a passing quality gate when it fails.
The known broken CS Demo frontend is rejected while a valid split-module frontend, existing provider contracts, and kernel route guards pass.

quality_metrics.measure: formal provider and delivery route preservation
quality_metrics.target: kernel and provider contract tests pass without a new generation or delivery path
quality_metrics.method: existing kernel and formal provider test profiles

quality_metrics.measure: independent language-aware validation of generated component and merged-project interfaces
quality_metrics.target: all newly generated and reused components plus the merged project have passing quality-validation receipts; injected missing imports, invalid re-exports, missing modules, and unimported sibling helpers are rejected
quality_metrics.method: deterministic interface tests, cached-component revalidation tests, broken CS Demo regression fixture, and targeted provider/kernel regression profiles

prevention: Confirm acceptance, interfaces, and applicable kernel constraints before implementation.
assurance: Review method, schema, skill, and repository instruction consistency.
Validate that support artifacts cannot authorize formal delivery PASS.
Review changed files against the kernel contract before integration.
control: Run targeted kernel and knowledge tests.
improvement: Record review findings and one bounded improvement experiment.

interface_expectations: Provider component files enter validate_generated_component_quality after semantic review and before checkpoint PASS or downstream feedforward.
Checkpoint-reused components are revalidated from current file content; a failed receipt invalidates reuse and routes the same component through regeneration.
The merged file set enters validate_assembled_project_quality before the provider generation quality gate can report pass.
Quality-validation receipts remain support artifacts and do not replace canonical test, runtime, visual, package, or public-delivery evidence.

feedback: 149 provider/interface/kernel regressions and 17 project-management quality tests passed.
Independent component and assembled-project quality validation now blocks invalid modules before downstream feedforward or generation success.
The historical CS Demo frontend is rejected for its missing facade binding and two unimported sibling helper calls.

worked: A language-aware support receipt reused the existing Provider route and checkpoints without adding a generation or delivery path.
Exact JavaScript import/export bindings made the interface registry useful for both librarian feedforward and deterministic validation.
did_not_work: The initial formal browser evidence had proven that screenshot-only quality was insufficient; module validation needed to become a blocking generation step rather than another advisory report.
experiments: Extend the quality adapter registry to real compiler or linker probes for additional generated languages only when their toolchains are declared and available.
